items.title: Daryl Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2024
items.q: requests something from “Kinky Boots” or Taylor Swift

ctx.x: I started playing as much Fats Waller as I could, and I have a few things that — I knew Dick Wellstood and I know enough about stride playing to know that I could never pull it off, it’s just too many notes and you know, too much precision. And — but later on he was really getting into the American Songbook and he brought songbooks with him. I used to go hear him a lot. And Sinatra. And particularly in this day and age post- pandemic and whatever, it’s kind of a challenge insofar as just bringing people back to…
Nice. What do you do if someone comes up to you and requests something from “Kinky Boots” or Taylor Swift or —

I just mentioned to someone, I’m at a loss, I have to admit. Just, even older shows, I have something, probably one of the most enduring Broadway shows is “Wicked” and I saw it and I did understand why it should endure, because the kids can connect and it is interesting to learn what the wicked witch used to be, and she wasn’t really wicked. And then I loved it. And I’ve heard the song a zillion times. There are songs like that from these pop shows I cannot remember. They just sound all the same. You know I can…
